test_title: SSC MTS Previous Year Paper (Held on: 7 July 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
**Direction: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

He had begun to dig / diligent along the / low tideline and had / captured two clams.
solution:
Here the erroneous part is **"diligent along the."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in Part (diligent along the) of the sentence.
 
• The word "diligent" is an adjective.
 
• We need an adverb form of the word "diligent" to make the sentence grammatically correct.
 
• An adverb is a word that modifies (describes) a verb (he sings loudly), an adjective (very tall), another adverb (ended too quickly), or even a whole sentence.
 
• Adverbs often end in -ly, but some (such as fast) look exactly the same as their adjective counterparts. 
 
• The adverb form of "diligent" is "diligently."
 
• Therefore, the use of 'diligent' should be replaced with 'diligently' to modify the verb "dig" to make the sentence grammatically correct.
 
• So, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 ​

Correct sentence__: *He had begun to dig __**diligently along the**__ low tideline and had captured two clams.*
